claims.statement: Treat the first rounds as a difficult setup: the guide cites a single starting carrier, weak early production/resources for technology, and limited early plastic, despite four commodities.
claims.conditions: Starting units, slice, trade partners and objective deck determine the severity; use this as the episode's opening assessment.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264 (2022), post-Codex-3 Omega-Xxcha discussion; current compatibility not verified.
claims.uncertainty: Podcast assessment and transcript are historical; no present-day setup audit.

claims.statement: Prioritize scoring early enough to unlock Xxekir Grom; the speakers target the end of round two when feasible and warn that unlocking by round three is a materially slower start.
claims.conditions: Requires scoring the required public and secret objectives; objective availability and table pressure can make the timing unattainable.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264's then-new Codex-3 hero context; errata/current edition not verified.
claims.uncertainty: The round-two target is aspirational guide advice, not a guaranteed outcome.

claims.statement: Xxekir Grom combines a planet's printed resource and influence values when Xxcha exhausts it for a spend, treating the total as both resources and influence; this applies to objective spending and votes.
claims.conditions: Apply only to qualifying spends under the hero text described in the episode.
claims.compatibility: Hero interpretation in a 2022 post-Codex-3 guide; rules and errata not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: Transcript paraphrase is not rules authority; verify exact current wording.

claims.statement: Do not treat the hero as added production capacity or as changing printed planet values for commander unlocks and unrelated effects; the guide says the commander requires planets with 12 combined printed influence.
claims.conditions: Separate planet spending from production and effects that inspect inherent planet values; the episode says Xxcha begins with four influence toward the unlock.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264's hero/commander reading; current rule text not audited.
claims.uncertainty: Use the current official wording for edge cases.

claims.statement: Choose a secret objective with a credible round-one or round-two scoring route when possible, because early scoring advances the hero unlock.
claims.conditions: Inspect the map and secret's actual requirements; a threatened-planet secret or other immediately achievable secret is only useful if it can really be scored.
claims.compatibility: Objective strategy from the 2022 guide; deck and rules mix not verified.
claims.uncertainty: The source itself says missing the round-two target does not end the game.

claims.statement: Do not prioritize the Custodians point over scoring objectives for the hero condition; the speakers say it does not count toward that unlock.
claims.conditions: Applies to the hero prerequisite as described in the episode.
claims.compatibility: Historical guide claim; present rules wording not independently verified.
claims.uncertainty: A special map or house rule could change the strategic calculation, not the cited prerequisite.

claims.statement: Diplomacy is a frequent preferred opening because its primary can refresh planets and Xxcha can use Peace Accords to gain an adjacent unoccupied planet after resolving either the primary or secondary.
claims.conditions: Peace Accords excludes Mecatol Rex and requires an unoccupied planet adjacent to one Xxcha controls; taking the card is distinct from following its secondary.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264; current Diplomacy/Peace Accords wording not checked.
claims.uncertainty: The guide sees high value but emphasizes map and timing dependence.

claims.statement: Use Xxcha's agent primarily to ready one of its own planets; the speakers consider removing another player's infantry to ready their planet rarely worthwhile.
claims.conditions: The value depends on which planet can be refreshed and what resource or influence spend remains available.
claims.compatibility: Agent discussion in SCPT 264; exact current leader text not verified.
claims.uncertainty: The second clause is the hosts' strategic judgment.

claims.statement: Diplomacy's value compounds with the hero and exploration attachments: refreshing improved planets can create repeated high-value spending opportunities.
claims.conditions: Requires accessible planets, useful attachments and timing that allows a refreshed planet to be spent; balance against exposure and opportunity cost.
claims.compatibility: Strategic interaction described for the source-era hero and exploration rules; current compatibility not checked.
claims.uncertainty: The episode gives illustrative examples and enthusiasm, not a guaranteed yield.

claims.statement: Prefer Trade when the visible payout from commodities, neighbors or an objective is strong; compare that known income with Diplomacy's less visible but potentially higher upside.
claims.conditions: Table composition, first-pick timing and willingness to trade determine the comparison; do not assume deals will occur.
claims.compatibility: Opening-card advice from SCPT 264; table/economy assumptions vary.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts explicitly preserve Trade as a good choice in high-value situations.

claims.statement: Leadership is not a routine pick in the hosts' plan; an early Lead from the Front objective is their named exception.
claims.conditions: Reassess when public objectives require command tokens or the table's card selection changes the value.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264 opening evaluation; objective deck mix not verified.
claims.uncertainty: The episode gives a narrow situational opinion, not a universal ranking.

claims.statement: Politics usually falls behind Diplomacy, but can be justified when speaker order and known next-round objectives materially improve scoring or when a constrained secret makes its cards useful.
claims.conditions: The source's examples include discarding five action cards or setting up a score; weigh this against other secondaries and taking Diplomacy.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264's historical strategy-card discussion.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts debate the edge cases and do not settle on Politics as a normal pick.

claims.statement: Imperial in round two can enable a second public-objective score and draw a second secret, improving the chance of scoring three objectives by the agenda phase if Xxcha prepares two stage ones.
claims.conditions: This is a conditional listener proposal endorsed by the hosts; it depends on Imperial being available, speaker order and having two scoreable stage-one objectives. Drawing a second secret improves the chance to score a secret; the draw itself is not a point.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264, with then-current objective/hero assumptions.
claims.uncertainty: Not guaranteed; the speakers say round-two Imperial is not commonly selected in their experience, and the extra secret is only another candidate to score.

claims.statement: Warfare is often better taken by another player so Xxcha can use the secondary if it needs more expansion; taking the primary is a specific response to a control objective or poor access.
claims.conditions: Map, carrier count, card order and available secondaries matter; a nearby multi-planet system can make the secondary valuable.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264 opening advice.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts describe Warfare as awkward for Xxcha rather than categorically bad.

claims.statement: Technology is not an automatic round-one pick, and ordinary double-teching can leave Xxcha short on early ships; prioritize it when an objective, slice or timing need makes the purchase worthwhile.
claims.conditions: A rich opening or technology objective can change the choice; taking Technology can also save resources compared with following its secondary.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264 guide-era strategy; exact current technology prerequisites not checked here.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers offer a counterargument for taking Technology when timing and ship funds matter.

claims.statement: The agent and Peace Accords are distinct tools: the agent readies a planet, while resolving Diplomacy can also satisfy Peace Accords to gain an adjacent empty planet.
claims.conditions: Check Peace Accords' adjacency, occupancy and Mecatol restrictions independently of whether Diplomacy was taken or followed.
claims.compatibility: Episode interpretation, not current rules verification.
claims.uncertainty: ASR may distort component names; IDs are resolved against the supplied component reference.

claims.statement: Instinct Training and Nullification Field are situational late-game faction technologies, not the core plan; their strategy-pool token costs feel easier only after Xxcha's economy develops.
claims.conditions: Instinct Training may fit an action-card-heavy game; Nullification Field may help when ships need to leave home, but opponents can bypass it. A useful skip and tactical need improve the case.
claims.compatibility: Faction-tech discussion under the source-era Codex-3 faction sheet; current tech text not verified.
claims.uncertainty: Both exhaust when used and are limited by readiness; the guide describes counters and timing uncertainty.

claims.statement: Concentrating planet value under the hero can reduce how many planets Xxcha needs to protect as late-game risk rises.
claims.conditions: Depends on valuable planets, access, refresh timing, map and opponent reach.
claims.compatibility: Illustrative strategic observation in SCPT 264.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers describe this as an ideal situation, not a guaranteed defense outcome.

claims.statement: Quash is a situational agenda veto: spend a strategy-pool command token to discard a revealed agenda and reveal a replacement; preserve tokens before the late game.
claims.conditions: The guide suggests using it on harmful agendas and allows occasional fishing for a point-granting agenda, while warning against indiscriminate repeated quashes.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264's post-Codex-3 assessment; current timing and ability wording not checked.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts differ slightly on the amount of agenda fishing worth doing.

claims.statement: Political Favor is difficult to sell because it duplicates Xxcha's Quash; usually keep it unless another player offers an unusually good deal or needs it immediately.
claims.conditions: Value depends on agenda knowledge and the buyer's urgency.
claims.compatibility: Promissory-note analysis in SCPT 264; current rules not verified.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers call the sale case rare and context-specific.

claims.statement: The guide advises against casually giving away Xxcha's Alliance after the hero change, arguing that Xxcha's own agenda-phase vote power is now much larger than the old shared-vote bargain.
claims.conditions: Reassess based on alliance text, current hero rules, negotiation value and political commitments in the actual game.
claims.compatibility: Explicitly compares pre-Codex-3 and post-Codex-3 expectations in a 2022 guide; current compatibility not checked.
claims.uncertainty: This is table-market advice, not a categorical rule; historical source-era assumptions are central.

claims.statement: A red-leaning War Sun plan can turn Xxcha's later cash into movement, bombardment and a substantial fleet for defense or win-slay, addressing weak production and movement.
claims.conditions: Treat as a mid/late-game plan; it depends on surviving early, building production capacity and having enough time and resources.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264 guide-era plan; no present-day rules verification.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers are enthusiastic but acknowledge poor early tempo and no guaranteed unlock or build timing.

claims.statement: The proposed red route starts with AI Development Algorithm, then considers Plasma Scoring or Self-Assembly Routines according to immediate use; a red skip can accelerate War Suns.
claims.conditions: Plasma is more attractive with bombardment or a PDS plan; Self-Assembly can add a mech outside production capacity. Prioritize whichever helps the current board.
claims.compatibility: Technology route proposed by SCPT 264; tech requirements and current rules not checked.
claims.uncertainty: The source says AI Development may be replaced by Psychoarchaeology when the slice has the needed skips.

claims.statement: War Suns support a longer closeout by giving Xxcha force to contest late scoring and win-slay while it waits for a favorable stage-two opportunity.
claims.conditions: Use when the game is likely to continue and the investment produces enough fleet power to affect leaders; coordinate with point tempo.
claims.compatibility: Strategic closeout advice in SCPT 264.
claims.uncertainty: The source discusses round five/six as a common horizon, not a rules or tournament guarantee.

claims.statement: Cruiser II can bridge Xxcha's movement gap and support timely point denial while it waits for a larger fleet plan; the hosts rank it ahead of PDS II for broad usefulness.
claims.conditions: Choose based on the map, targets, opponent tempo and whether the upgrade helps this round; it is a stopgap, not an automatic detour.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264 technology assessment; current upgrade details not verified.
claims.uncertainty: The guide's ranking is experience-based and board-dependent.

claims.statement: PDS II with Xxcha's flagship and additional PDS can deter attacks and support defense or a win-slay; Construction makes the route more attractive when structures also score.
claims.conditions: Use when the objective deck, construction access and defensive geography repay the investment; the guide says the mechs alone are not a strong substitute.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264 strategy advice; current unit/technology text not audited.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts still favor Cruiser II in more situations and describe PDS investment as conditional.

claims.statement: Blue technology is a fallback when movement, map skips or production facilities justify it; the speakers prefer the red War Sun route in ordinary conditions, while Space Dock II is a luxury that can improve a blue plan.
claims.conditions: A blue skip or unusually strong production setup can change the comparison; do not assume carrier upgrades solve a large cash-to-plastic mismatch by themselves.
claims.compatibility: Historical strategic comparison in SCPT 264.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts present blue as viable in good circumstances but less aligned with their default plan.

claims.statement: Scanlink Drone Network is an optional exploration route the hosts enjoy for attachment hunting, particularly early enough for finds to repay the technology; late acquisition is a desperate, deck-dependent gamble.
claims.conditions: Consider remaining exploration tokens, already explored planets, attachment value and how many scoring rounds remain.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264 guide-era exploration advice; current component rules not verified.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers explicitly distinguish personal enjoyment from optimality.

claims.statement: Expect neighbors to resist helping Xxcha early once they recognize the hero payoff; build enough plastic and consider diplomacy or a PDS deterrent to avoid being an easy target.
claims.conditions: The guide expects the faction to become much stronger later, but whether the table refuses deals or attacks depends on players and map.
claims.compatibility: Table-meta forecast in a 2022 podcast, not a rules claim.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers present this as a prediction about evolving player behavior.

claims.statement: Track point tempo and choose between a fast objective route and a longer recovery game; if a round-five finish is slipping, prepare early to extend the game and contest another scoring window.
claims.conditions: A longer game requires enough fleet power and table coordination to stop opponents while Xxcha converts its later economy into points.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 264 closeout strategy; round timing is contextual.
claims.uncertainty: The episode says the shift can begin around round three but does not promise Xxcha can force it.

claims.statement: Mecatol Rex plus Imperial is a possible catch-up line, but the hosts worry it may require repeated Imperial access and speaker control; do not rely on it as the sole plan.
claims.conditions: Evaluate the board, speaker order, remaining scoring opportunities and whether Xxcha can keep the game alive.
claims.compatibility: Source-era strategic judgment; current objective and card mix not checked.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts disagree in emphasis and present the route alongside a longer War Sun/win-slay plan.

claims.statement: Opponents can counter Xxcha by withholding early help, coordinating votes against decisive agendas and denying it both agenda outcomes; the hosts think full-table exclusion may be unrealistic.
claims.conditions: Coordination, available votes and each player's incentives determine whether this works; Xxcha may try to divide the table.
claims.compatibility: Podcast table advice, not a deterministic counter or current-rules review.
claims.uncertainty: This is explicitly a meta prediction and the speakers question whether five opponents can coordinate fully.

connections.conditions: Resolving either Diplomacy primary or secondary is the trigger described in the faction ability; Peace Accords still requires an eligible adjacent empty planet.
The agent can ready a planet so Xxcha may make another qualifying spend with the hero, if timing and planet availability allow.
Diplomacy refreshes planets; the hero increases their combined value when exhausted for qualifying spends.
The hero improves vote spends and the commander adds a vote per planet, as the source interprets their combined agenda-phase impact; unlock requirements remain separate.
The proposed route uses AI Development Algorithm as an entry toward later technology choices including War Suns; a red skip can change the sequence.
War Suns are an expensive way to convert the late economy described by the hero into military reach, if Xxcha survives to build them.
Cruiser II can provide movement and point denial as a stopgap while the War Sun plan is still developing.
The guide describes PDS II and the flagship together as a deterrent when Xxcha has the investment and geography to support it.
Scanlink can increase the chance of finding attachments that improve planet values for later hero spending; it is worthwhile only when exploration timing and draws justify the detour.
